title: FS Workflows
summary: Connecting React and Django end to end: Axios calls to DRF, token log-in that survives a page refresh (localStorage), protected pages and DRF permissions, and full CRUD from the front end with every record scoped to the logged-in user. Same day as the Personal Project kickoff. Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Log a user in from React, keep them logged in across refreshes, and let them create, read, update and delete only their own data through the Django API.

steps.title: Trace a logged-in request in Netflix
steps.detail: Run your Netflix app, open Chrome DevTools, go to the Network tab, and add a title to My List. Click the request and look at its headers. Supabase sends your session token in an Authorization header; with DRF the idea is the same, only the token type changes.
steps.doneWhen: You find the Authorization header on one request (don't copy the token anywhere).

steps.title: Read DRF permissions
steps.detail: Read the IsAuthenticated part of the DRF permissions guide.
steps.doneWhen: You can say what happens when a logged-out user calls an IsAuthenticated view (a 401 or 403).

steps.title: Read MDN's Authorization header page
steps.detail: Read how the browser sends credentials with each request. This is the header your Axios calls will set.
steps.doneWhen: You can write the header for a DRF token and for a Bearer token.

concepts.meaning: A JavaScript library for HTTP requests; you can preset its base URL and headers.
Browser storage that survives a refresh; used here to keep the token.
A page that only shows when the user is logged in.
Each query returns only the rows that belong to the current user.
